digest.headline: Fox completes 22 billion dollar acquisition of streaming platform Roku
digest.lead: Fox Corporation has finalised its purchase of Roku to bolster its digital operations in North America. Meanwhile, the UK Culture Secretary has launched a formal regulatory review into Sky's proposed 1.6 billion pound acquisition of ITV's broadcasting unit as both regions navigate significant shifts in media ownership and infrastructure.

glance.text: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy launched a formal review into Sky's £1.6bn acquisition of ITV's broadcasting arm.
ITVX surpassed its entire 2025 streaming total in ten months after reaching 3.6 billion streams.
Channel 4 cancelled Married at First Sight UK following an external review into contributor welfare.
Sky Sports expanded low-latency Real Time viewing across all sports channels on Sky Glass and Stream.
Sky Sports partnered with Sir Gareth Southgate's 1071 Media to produce digital football content.
Vodafone launched Pro 4 broadband across CityFibre's network, offering speeds up to 8Gbps.
The UK government confirmed it has no plans to slow down AI data centre construction.
Fox Corporation completed its 22 billion dollar acquisition of Roku, integrating the platform into Fox Digital Platforms.
Meta, Google and TikTok sued California to block a social media law restricting features for minors under 16.
BCE reported a 9.7 percent rise in Bell Media revenue for Q3 2026 as Crave reached 5.15 million subscribers.
NBC News led primetime broadcast ratings during the 2026 midterm election night coverage.
OpenAI pledged to end non-disclosure agreements for data centre projects following election backlash over AI infrastructure.
The Canadian federal budget allocated 300 million dollars in additional funding for public broadcaster CBC/Radio-Canada over two years.
Titan OS raised 46 million dollars in new financing to expand its connected television operating system.

paragraphs: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has triggered a formal intervention in Sky's £1.6bn takeover of ITV's broadcasting business. The move directs Ofcom and the Competition and Markets Authority to examine the deal. Rivals including Channel 4 and Paramount welcomed the regulatory scrutiny.

Channel 4 has permanently cancelled Married at First Sight UK after an external review into contributor welfare. Chief Executive Priya Dogra confirmed the budget will be reinvested into new original programming. The decision follows serious allegations made by female participants during production.

ITV reported that streaming platform ITVX delivered 3.6 billion streams by 30 October. This performance beat its full-year 2025 streaming total within just ten months. Drama releases, soaps and an expanding FAST offering drove the accelerated growth.

Sky Sports partnered with Sir Gareth Southgate's production company 1071 Media to produce football content. The deal will deliver long-form and social programming featuring analysis and topical chat for digital audiences.

ITV commissioned original thriller series Nightswimming from Two Brothers Pictures. The commercial broadcaster also extended its anti-piracy contract with Friend MTS for two years to protect live events on ITV4.

Sky rolled out low-latency Real Time viewing across all Sky Sports channels on Sky Glass and Sky Stream. The update reduces internet broadcast delays to keep live sports coverage aligned with real-time action.

Vodafone launched its Pro 4 broadband package on CityFibre's full-fibre network. The service provides internet speeds reaching 8Gbps alongside WiFi 7 routers. Meanwhile, UK ministers confirmed AI data centres remain essential infrastructure despite local protests.
Fox Corporation has completed its acquisition of Roku for 22 billion dollars. The transaction brings the streaming platform into Fox Digital Platforms alongside Tubi and FOX One.
In data centre infrastructure, Crusoe sold its troubled Wyoming data centre project to Google. The sale underscores the ongoing operational challenges of expanding massive AI facilities.

Meta, Google and TikTok have filed a lawsuit against California to block Assembly Bill 1709. The law prohibits social media platforms from offering addictive feeds and autoplay videos to users under 16.

Following midterm election opposition to data centre expansions, OpenAI committed to ending non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Meta also warned that growing political pushback against infrastructure projects could hinder future artificial intelligence investments.
In Canada, the federal government announced 300 million dollars in additional funding for CBC/Radio-Canada over two years as part of a broader arts and culture budget.

BCE announced its third-quarter financial results for 2026, showing a 9.7 percent revenue increase at Bell Media. Crave subscriptions grew to 5.15 million, supported by sports broadcasts and digital expansion.

Quebecor reported a 69.7 percent jump in media adjusted EBITDA for Q3. Growth was driven by TVA Group, which expanded its television market share to 43.5 percent and secured a 12-year French-language NHL rights extension.
Nexstar reported record third-quarter net revenue of 2.13 billion dollars, up 78 percent year-over-year. The growth was boosted by its Tegna acquisition and political advertising revenue.

NBC News earned the highest overall audience among broadcast networks for its 2026 midterm election night coverage. Fox News topped total cable viewership during primetime, while CNN led the key demographic.
HBO series The Gilded Age recorded its highest season premiere ratings to date, averaging nearly 4 million viewers across platforms over its first three days.
